note: Rewritten from the English description by Snyder (1924); the original is in English. This is Snyder's morphological re-examination of the female type of A. ater (Hagen 1858, Brazil) made while comparing it with the type specimens of A. fumosus and A. tenebrosus; it is not a complete original description, and the original gives no measurements, so this entry has no measurements.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: A small, dark species with short mandibles; compared with A. fumosus it is smaller, darker and has shorter mandibles, the postclypeus is less strongly bilobed than in the latter, the fontanelle lies farther back than in the latter, and the frontal suture is less distinct than in the latter.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Female (type, M.C.Z. No. 208, Brazil): body small, dark, mandibles short. Eyes projecting and conspicuous. Postclypeus pale brown, slightly raised, bilobed, posterior margin convex, more than twice as wide as long. Fontanelle a small, inconspicuous spot in the depression behind the eyes, situated nearer the posterior margin than in A. fumosus. Frontal suture less distinct than in A. fumosus. Mandibles red to black at the apex, yellowish brown at the base, projecting slightly beyond the labrum. Ocelli large and conspicuous, the distance to the eye about equal to their long diameter.
